Package edu.brandeis.cosi.atg

package edu.brandeis.cosi.atg
This library contains interfaces and type definitions for Automation: The Game (ATG). ATG is derived from the popular card game Dominion, and is used for a semester-long programming project in Cosi-103a at Brandeis University.

Architecture Overview
This library provides a framework for implementing and running games of ATG. The primary components are:
  • Engine: Implements game logic and turn management via the Engine interface.
  • Player: Implements player decision-making via the Player interface.
  • State: Represents game state via immutable records in the edu.brandeis.cosi.atg.state package.
  • Decisions: Encapsulates player choices via sealed interface types in the edu.brandeis.cosi.atg.decisions package.
  • Cards: Defines card types and attributes via Card.

Design Principles
This library enforces a strict separation between the Engine and Players:
  • Players cannot directly manipulate game state—they only choose from presented decisions.
  • The Engine is responsible for validating decisions and updating state.
  • All game state is immutable, ensuring consistency and safety.
  • All required parameters are validated with Objects.requireNonNull(T), providing clear error messages.

Communication Pattern
The Engine and Player interact through a single method: Player.makeDecision(edu.brandeis.cosi.atg.state.GameState, com.google.common.collect.ImmutableList<edu.brandeis.cosi.atg.decisions.Decision>). The Engine provides the current game state and a list of valid decisions, and the Player returns their chosen decision. The Engine then executes this decision and updates the game state accordingly.
